The local covariance formula, its six-row fixed-count sum, endpoint sign transitions, and peak/valley cancellation follow by exact algebra. A standalone checker has passed 32,802 exact assertions, including exhaustive independent permutation enumeration through n=8; its finite scope is not substituted for the all-n proof.

value.rationale: Length three is the first complete ordinal-pattern system containing peaks and valleys. The six rank-resolved local covariance laws give a finite-sample structural description of how diagonal fixed-point contacts bias local ordering, including four positional sign changes and an exact cancellation on pooling peaks/valleys. These distinct local effects are absent from classical total-count generating functions and are relevant to comparing simultaneous permutation randomness summaries. No unproved downstream power claim is required.
